name: Danshen (Salvia miltiorrhiza)
short: Case reports: severe over-anticoagulation and bleeding when people on warfarin also took danshen. In volunteers, one danshen combination altered warfarin handling; another did not.
text: For warfarin, a review describes three published cases of gross over-anticoagulation and bleeding complications in patients on long-term warfarin who also took danshen, notes that danshen affects haemostasis in several ways (including inhibiting platelet aggregation) and, in rat studies, raised warfarin levels and exaggerated its anticoagulant effect; the reviewers concluded that danshen should be avoided in patients taking warfarin. Individual case reports describe profound anticoagulation caused by an interaction between warfarin and danshen in a patient who had undergone mitral valve replacement, and danshen-induced overcoagulation with severe, dangerous clotting abnormalities in a patient with rheumatic heart disease, in a report titled as being about warfarin potentiation by danshen (the abstracts do not say whether these are among the three cases the review counts). Studies of combination products in healthy volunteers are mixed: in 14 volunteers, a danshen-plus-gegen (Pueraria) product produced significant pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions with warfarin and with aspirin, whereas in 24 volunteers a danshen-plus-sanqi product added for 7 days did not raise the INR, and the authors concluded it had no effect on warfarin's steady-state pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. A review of danshen's effects on drug-metabolising enzymes notes that adverse-effect reports for danshen preparations are rare but that tanshinone-rich preparations inhibit or induce several CYP450 enzymes, so precautions are needed for CYP-related interactions. For a purified danshen salt product given by infusion, a prospective surveillance study in 30,180 inpatients at 36 hospitals found adverse events in 6.40%, adverse events related to the product in 1.57% (including 9 kinds not on the approved label) and adverse drug reactions in 0.79%. A Cochrane review of danshen preparations for heart attack (the abstract does not give the route) said their safety is unproven, although some adverse events have been reported.
